name: MCP6022T-I_SN
title: Rail-to-rail input/output 10 MHz CMOS op amps: MCP6021, MCP6021R, MCP6022, MCP6023, MCP6024
summary: A family of CMOS operational amplifiers for single supplies of 2.5 V to 5.5 V whose inputs and outputs both reach the rails. Each amplifier gives 10 MHz of gain bandwidth and 7 V/µs at about 1 mA, with 8.7 nV/√Hz noise at 10 kHz, picoamp bias current and very low distortion, and is stable at unity gain. The MCP6022 is the dual; the singles MCP6021 and MCP6023 add a mid-supply reference pin, the MCP6023 a chip-select shutdown, and the MCP6024 is the quad.

circuits.title: Transimpedance amplifier for an optical detector
circuits.description: A photodetector, modelled as a current source with 100 pF of capacitance across it, drives the inverting input. The 100 kΩ feedback resistor turns detector current into output voltage; the 5.6 pF capacitor across it keeps the loop stable and flattens the response to a bandwidth of 370 kHz. The non-inverting input sits at VDD/2.

circuits.title: Input protection with clamp diodes
circuits.description: Two diodes from the inputs up to VDD keep the input pins from being driven far above the positive rail; D1 on the non-inverting input, D2 on the inverting input.

circuits.title: Input protection with series resistors and clamp diodes
circuits.description: As the clamp-diode circuit, with R1 and R2 in series with the two inputs. The resistors cap the current into or out of each input pin and through the internal ESD diodes and D1, D2; diode current returns through VDD or VSS. Size the smaller resistor so that 2 mA is not exceeded for the most negative input below VSS and the most positive input above VDD.

circuits.title: Series output resistor for a large capacitive load
circuits.description: A unity-gain follower drives load capacitance CL through RISO. Feedback is taken before the resistor, so at high frequency the amplifier sees a resistive load and keeps its phase margin. Pick RISO from the recommended-RISO curve against CL/GN, then check peaking and overshoot and adjust.

circuits.title: Non-inverting gain stage with parasitic input capacitance
circuits.description: A non-inverting amplifier with gain set by RF and RG. CG is not a fitted part: it stands for the amplifier's common-mode input capacitance plus board capacitance at the inverting input. With RG it raises high-frequency gain and costs phase margin, which limits the largest usable RF (curve against noise gain).

circuits.title: AC-coupled non-inverting gain stage biased from VREF (MCP6021, MCP6023)
circuits.description: The signal reaches the non-inverting input through the DC-blocking capacitor CB; the internal mid-supply VREF pin biases that input. RF and RG set the gain, RG returning to ground. CB also lowers noise by coupling the input to the source.

parts.note: MCP6021 or MCP6023, not the SOT-23-5

circuits.title: Inverting gain stage referenced to VREF (MCP6021, MCP6023)
circuits.description: An inverting amplifier, gain -RF/RG, whose non-inverting input is tied to the internal mid-supply VREF pin. CB from VREF to ground filters supply noise that would otherwise reach the output.

parts.note: MCP6021 or MCP6023, not the SOT-23-5

circuits.title: Unused amplifiers in the MCP6024
circuits.description: Two ways to park a spare amplifier so its output does not toggle and couple into its neighbours. Amplifier A is a follower of the R1, R2 divider (minimum noise gain); the divider sets any reference inside the output range and the buffered output can serve as a reference, VREF = VDD × R2/(R1 + R2). Amplifier B has its non-inverting input on VDD and its inverting input on ground and its output open: fewest parts, run as a comparator, possibly drawing more current.

circuits.title: A/D converter driver and anti-aliasing filter, 20 kHz
circuits.description: A third-order Butterworth low-pass filter, 20 kHz bandwidth, built round a unity-gain follower: an RC pole (8.45 kΩ, 1.2 nF) ahead of a Sallen-Key section (14.7 kΩ, 33.2 kΩ, 1.0 nF to the output, 100 pF to ground). Step response is reasonable; attenuation is 29 dB at 60 kHz, suiting converters sampling at 80 ksps or faster. Multiplying every capacitor, or every resistor, by one common factor moves the bandwidth.

circuits.title: AC and DC test circuit, non-inverting gain
circuits.description: The circuit most non-inverting characteristics are measured in: input through RN (1 kΩ) to the non-inverting input, gain of +2 set by RF and RG (2 kΩ each) with RG returned to VDD/2, and the output loaded by CL (60 pF) to ground and RL (10 kΩ) to VL. VDD is bypassed by 0.1 µF and 1 µF.

circuits.title: AC and DC test circuit, inverting gain
circuits.description: The circuit most inverting characteristics are measured in: VDD/2 through RN (1 kΩ) to the non-inverting input, input through RG (2 kΩ) to the inverting input with RF (2 kΩ) feedback for a gain of -1, and the output loaded by CL (60 pF) to ground and RL (10 kΩ) to VL. VDD is bypassed by 0.1 µF and 1 µF.

operation.text: MCP6021 (single), MCP6021R (single, SOT-23-5 with the supply pins swapped), MCP6022 (dual), MCP6023 (single with chip select) and MCP6024 (quad) are CMOS op amps with rail-to-rail inputs and outputs, a 10 MHz gain bandwidth, unity-gain stability and a 2.5 V to 5.5 V supply. Industrial grade (I) is rated -40°C to +85°C and Extended (E) -40°C to +125°C; E parts carry the tighter offset limit. MCP6022T-I/SN is the dual in the 8-pin SOIC, industrial grade, on tape and reel.
VDD sits 2.5 V to 5.5 V above VSS, and in normal use every other pin stays between the two. Most designs run single-supply with VSS at ground. Each amplifier draws about 1 mA.

Two CMOS differential pairs work side by side, one covering low common-mode voltages and one high, so the input range reaches 0.3 V past each rail. The output does not reverse phase when an input is driven beyond the supplies.

ESD diodes on each input clamp a pin that goes more than a diode drop below VSS, and voltages well above VDD. Their breakdown leaves normal operation alone but does not protect against slow overvoltage above VDD; fast ESD events within the rating do no harm. Appreciable current flows out of an input whose voltage is below VSS (input current against input voltage curve). Where inputs can be overdriven, external diodes to VDD and series resistors holding pin current under 2 mA protect them.
With RL = 10 kΩ the output gets within 20 mV of either rail; headroom grows with load current and temperature.

Load capacitance erodes phase margin and bandwidth, giving gain peaking and step overshoot. Beyond about 60 pF at G = +1, a small resistor RISO in series with the output, outside the feedback loop, restores stability at some cost in bandwidth. Choose it from the curve of recommended RISO against CL/GN, then confirm peaking and overshoot on the bench or with the SPICE model and adjust.

Capacitance from the inverting input to ground (the input's own common-mode capacitance plus board strays, CG) lifts high-frequency gain for non-inverting gains above 1 and lowers phase margin in both inverting and non-inverting stages. The largest usable RF depends on noise gain and CG. The pulse-response curves use RF = 1 kΩ to avoid peaking.

CS high shuts the amplifier and the VREF divider down: supply current falls to about 10 nA, flowing out through the CS pin to VSS, and the output goes high impedance. CS low turns it on in about 2 µs (10 µs max). An internal 5 MΩ pull-down holds CS low when it floats. The input is CMOS with Schmitt-trigger hysteresis of 0.6 V at 5 V.

Single amplifiers outside the SOT-23-5 bring out VREF, the midpoint of two 50 kΩ resistors across the supply, unbuffered, within ±50 mV of VDD/2. On the MCP6021 the divider's switch is tied on internally so VREF is always present; on the MCP6023 it follows CS. Leave VREF open if it is not needed. It can bias a non-inverting stage through a DC-blocking capacitor, or tie to the non-inverting input of an inverting stage with a capacitor to ground.

Place a 0.01 µF to 0.1 µF capacitor within 2 mm of VDD for high-frequency performance and a bulk capacitor of 1 µF or more within 100 mm; the bulk capacitor may be shared with other analog parts nearby.

Spare amplifiers in the MCP6024 should be connected so their outputs cannot toggle and cause crosstalk: either as a follower of a resistor divider, or with the inputs tied to the rails as a comparator, which uses fewer parts but may draw more current.

Humidity, dust and contamination leave about 10^12 Ω between nearby traces in dry conditions; 5 V across that drives 5 pA, more than the 1 pA typical bias current at 25°C. A guard ring around the sensitive pins, held at their voltage, reduces it. In a non-inverting or unity-gain stage tie the ring to VIN- (it then sits at the common-mode voltage) and bring the signal to VIN+ on a wire clear of the board surface. In inverting and transimpedance stages tie the ring to VIN+ (the reference, such as VDD/2 or ground) and bring the signal to VIN- on a wire clear of the board.

A continuous ground plane, with the bypass capacitors joined to it by the shortest possible traces, cuts inductive and capacitive coupling. Partition the board: analog apart from digital, fast circuits apart from slow ones, high-current apart from low-current. Route sensitive signals directly over little distance, clear of noisy parts and traces, which matters most for fast edges. A grounded guard trace on each side of a victim trace helps; a long guard is grounded at each end and at its midpoint. Coax or other low-inductance wiring brings signals and power to the board.
